To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the p10 gene of AcMNPV has two polyadenylation signals and that polyadenylation occurs in the downstream signal when the upstream signal is inactivated.

(a) the 3' region of the p10 gene contains a highly efficient polyadenylation motif, (b) the 3'-end processing of the p10 mRNA is essential for high-level expression of a foreign gene, and (c) the p10 polyadenylation signals are conserved in baculoviridae.
the p10 3'-UTR of baculoviridae has two polyadenylation signals, the downstream AATAA motif being used predominantly, but the ATTAAA motif is used when the AATAA motif is inactivated.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the importance of the polyadenylation process for the efficient expression of a foreign gene.
the identification of the polyadenylation motif of the p10 3'-UTR, and with the importance of the poly(A) signal for high-level expression of the p10 gene.
the role of the p10 3'UTR of baculoviridae in high-level expression and the conservation of this region in various baculovirus species.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the 3'UTR of the p10 mRNA plays a role in high-level expression, however this role is not due to the polyadenylation signal but rather due to the presence of a GT-rich sequence.
the GT-rich region in the p10 3'-untranslated region of Autographa california nucleopolyhedroviruses is essential to the high level of expression of p10 gene, but that polyadenylation is not.

polyadenylation of p10 is not essential for p10 gene function and that polyadenylation signals in the 3'-untranslated region are not essential for high levels of expression in the context of a p10 promoter.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the p10 3′ untranslated region (3′ UTR) of Autographa california nuclear polyhedrosis virus (AcMNPV) is important for high-level expression of the reporter chloramphenicol-acetyltransferase (cat) gene.
the baculovirus 3' UTRS have been optimized to provide high levels of gene expression and that the p10 3 UTR is the most effective in this respect.

polyadenylation is not the only determinant for the high-level expression of the p10 gene and that the p10 gene 3' U TR can be replaced without loss of high-level gene expression, as long as a polyadenylation signal is present in the new 3' U T R.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the p10 3’ UTR should be retained in recombinant baculoviridae to ensure high-level foreign gene expression.

the p10 3′ UTR is a very efficient polyadenylation signal, even when the canonical AATAAA motif is inactivated, and that it is important to include this 3′ URT in baculovirusexpression vectors to obtain high levels expression of foreign genes.
the SV40 terminator should be avoided in recombinant baculovirus vectors, and that the p10 3'-UTR should be included in such vectors.
